input.quote: d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.
input.rationale: The only ownership provision is one-directional: Section 2(d) confirms TrueLink retains ownership of the Interface (acceptable as Vendor background IP), but nothing in the Agreement confirms that Client retains all right, title and interest in Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property and the data it and its borrowers submit, and nothing addresses ownership of the results of the Support Services that Client pays for. The nearest support is confidentiality only (Sections 10(b) and 10(c), which deem "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" Client Proprietary Information) and a narrow termination-only statement in Section 13 that Client "shall retain full ownership of all domains associated with Client and Client Content" in case of discontinued Service. Confidential treatment and a termination-time carve-out are not ownership, and the Agreement gives Client no ownership of, or licence to, work product created for it, so it fails even the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free right to use, modify and sublicense deliverables). We have therefore inserted a reciprocal ownership clause at the preferred position, preserving TrueLink's platform rights and expressly subordinating our data ownership statement to the existing Section 8(d) licence so no conflict is created. Separately noted, not double-flagged here: the Section 8(d) licence permitting TrueLink to "resell, exploit" Credit Data is a licence rather than an assignment and is limited by the Non-Competition Agreement, so it is a data-use point rather than an ownership breach.

ops.text: e. Client Ownership. Client retains all right, title and interest in and to the Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, the Credit Data and all other data submitted by or on behalf of Client or its customers through the Interface or the Web Site (subject only to the license granted in Section 8(d)). All results of the Support Services and any other materials, work product or deliverables prepared by TrueLink for Client under this Agreement shall be the exclusive property of Client, and TrueLink hereby assigns to Client all right, title and interest therein; to the extent any TrueLink Intellectual Property is embedded in such results, TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the same as part of such results in the ordinary course of Client's business. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to TrueLink any ownership of the Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property or Client's data, and no item is jointly owned by the parties.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 2(d) confirms TrueLink's ownership of the Interface but the Agreement never confirms ours, so we have added a reciprocal clause: we retain all rights in Client Content, Client Intellectual Property and our data, and we own the results of the Support Services we pay for, with a licence back for any TrueLink IP embedded in them. Our playbook requires that we own what we pay for and everything we put in, while Vendor keeps its pre-existing platform.
proposal.summary: Add reciprocal ownership clause: Client retains all rights in its content, IP and data; Client owns Support Services work product with licence back for embedded TrueLink IP; no joint ownership.
